Since red flag findings obviate the conservative therapy prerequisite, the MRI was medically necessary per policy and clinical standards.", "arguments": [{"point": "The patient exhibited progressive motor deficit (foot drop) and sensory changes consistent with L5 radiculopathy, meeting the 'red flag' criterion for neurological deficit under CP-IMG-114(b), which eliminates the six-week conservative therapy requirement.", "support": [{"source": "policy", "ref": "P3", "quote": "OR (b) the member presents with \"red flag\" findings, including progressive or severe neurological deficit (e.g. motor weakness, foot drop, loss of reflexes)... Moderate central canal stenosis."}], "strength": "strong"}, {"point": "Under the Plan’s definition of medical necessity, a prudent physician would order an MRI in this setting to diagnose a compressive lesion causing progressive motor deficits, aligning with generally accepted standards of care for suspected radiculopathy with neurologic worsening.", "support": [{"source": "policy", "ref": "P4", "quote": "Medically Necessary means health care services that a prudent physician would provide to a patient to diagnose or treat an illness or injury in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice, clinically appropriate in type, frequency, extent and duration..."}], "strength": "moderate"}], "checklist": [{"item": "Copy of the insurer's Advanced Imaging Clinical Policy (CP-IMG-114)", "status": "have", "why": "To verify the exact red flag criteria and conservative therapy exceptions cited in the appeal."}, {"item": "Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Priya Raman", "status": "missing", "why": "Would strengthen the case by explicitly linking the clinical findings to the need for urgent imaging despite lack of six-week conservative trial."}, {"item": "Authorization or referral for the MRI", "status": "have", "why": "Confirms the treating provider ordered the test, satisfying P4.1 coverage requirement for provider-ordered diagnostic imaging."}], "legal_hooks": [{"name": "Internal Appeal Right", "applies_because": "P5 grants the member 180 days to file an internal appeal, and the appeal is being filed well within that window."}, {"name": "Peer-to-Peer Review Option", "applies_because": "P6 allows the treating provider to request a peer-to-peer discussion with the Plan's medical reviewer during the appeal process, offering an opportunity to clarify the red flag exception."}]}
